rv.q: The Urmetazoan is a small story of cosmic value.
This is an intelligent debut by Rugman.
There is merit and considerable potential but facts and characters require far greater integration to fully convince beyond a novice’s level.
Overall, a story that was riveting in parts and lukewarm in others.
Yet the evening is underwhelming, lacking in urgency.
Overall, Rugman’s debut play is sharp, compelling and thought-provoking, even if its ambition is occasionally constrained by repetition.
The Urmetazoan has already established a relationship between two sisters that is compelling to watch.
What has evolved is a very human story about letting go.
The show dedicates a bit of time to them all, never quite settling, so although the final scene is poignant enough, it is an uneven road getting there.

cn.t: Rugman's debut about estranged sisters reuniting before a one-way Mars mission earns praise for tender performances and compelling sci-fi themes, though critics find the family drama less engaging than its space exploration ideas.
